judgments.rationale: Normal quantiles, binomial counts for harvest-ready plants, and the conditional probability under the count restriction are all explicitly assessed statistical methods.
The asymptotes, intercepts, range and sketch are graph/function work; solving f(x)>x is a separately marked inequality, owned by Number and algebra.
Both parts assess graphing and transformations: the sketch of f and the horizontal stretch/vertical translation to obtain g; no inverse-function method is marked.
The first-rest condition uses differentiation of displacement, while total distance through the turning point requires integrating velocity; both are calculus applications.
The table is a discrete probability distribution and the marked work uses normalization and expectation to determine its parameter; the added function labels are not assessed.
The binomial variance equation and the variance under Y=1-2X are discrete-random-variable work; no separate generic probability-model method is needed.
The 4-mark cross-product calculation is explicitly vector work, while minimizing its squared norm and converting it to triangle area are triangle-geometry work; both skills are materially assessed.

Euler's approximation, solution of the differential equation and the error comparison are all organized around a differential-equation problem; integration is an inherent solution step rather than a separate assessed classification.
The rational-function sketch/transformation is primary; the intersections with the quadratic g require a materially assessed quadratic condition, owned by Number and algebra.
Factorization and partial-fraction algebra dominate the first stages; the later antiderivative and limiting argument are independently marked calculus work.
Complex expansion/roots and the Argand-diagram triangle area are both assessed; triangle geometry is therefore secondary to the complex-number primary.
Sector perimeter and area formulas in radians drive the work; the quadratic is an intermediate elimination/solution step rather than an independently dominant skill.
Finding the intersections uses a trigonometric identity, while the enclosed area is evaluated by definite integration; these are separate marked methods.
The solid volume is obtained from a disk integral of pi f(x)^2; rotational geometry is setup, not a separate topic.
The marked work is Maclaurin expansion and its limiting/series behavior; the trigonometric forms are inputs and Sequences and series would duplicate the calculus classification.
The mark scheme explicitly awards reflection in the x-axis and a 180-degree rotation about the origin, alongside graph transformation work.
Depreciation is modeled by powers and the least time is found from an exponential inequality using logarithms; no sequence method is assessed.
The tide model requires trigonometric parameter solving, and the rate question independently differentiates the model; these belong to trigonometry and calculus respectively.
Implicit differentiation supplies the main result, while solving the logarithmic equation is a distinct algebraic method owned by Number and algebra.
Dot and cross products establish the vectors and the resulting triangle area; the quadratic is only an intermediate computation.
The marks assess standardization and normal-distribution probabilities; descriptive-statistics and inverse-function labels are not independent outcomes here.
Direction changes and increasing displacement are identified from the velocity model, and displacement is obtained by integrating velocity; these are the explicit calculus applications.
The work fits/interprets a regression relationship and constructs the reverse regression estimate, which is descriptive statistical analysis rather than inference testing.
The pdf is integrated to normalize and locate the median; all materially assessed work is for a continuous random variable.
The primary task models a discrete waiting-time variable and its probabilities; differentiation and the geometric-series derivation are independently marked secondary methods.
Inflection points and the associated optimization drive the question; coordinate geometry is genuinely used for the line/intersection work as a secondary method.
The requested results use arithmetic and geometric sequence relationships and sums; logarithmic notation is given context, not a separately assessed logarithm method.
Plane normals, parallel/perpendicular conditions, vector line equations and distances are explicitly marked; both vector and coordinate-analytic skills belong to the geometry topic.
The induction proof and derivative calculations support the Maclaurin expansion; induction is a distinct Number-and-algebra proof method.
Substitution turns the exponential equation into a quadratic, which is the marked solving method; the exponential substitution and final form do not warrant a separate logarithm skill.
The midpoint, slope/vector equation and symmetry/area calculation explicitly use coordinate and vector geometry; the area arithmetic is not a separate triangle label.
The rational graph is primary, while the one-solution and two-solution conditions are obtained through a materially assessed quadratic intersection analysis.
Normal standardization supplies the tail probabilities and the final conditional probability is separately marked; generic probability-model and descriptive labels are unsupported.
Vieta/root relations for the polynomial and conjugate complex roots are both explicit, so complex numbers and polynomial theorems are retained.
The enclosed region is found from the intersections and a definite integral; no separate limits-and-series method is assessed.
Mode, probabilities, median and expected spending are all calculated from one continuous density; generic probability-model, integration and function labels are not needed.
Angular speed/radian measure and chord/triangle geometry are explicit; the sine rule is routine triangle work rather than a separate identity classification.
Euler/integrating-factor work and integration solve the differential equation, while the later trigonometric derivative/identity is independently marked.
The regression line through the mean point and the resulting data equations are descriptive-statistics work; no separate inference skill is required.
The decibel model is solved using logarithmic/exponential relationships; this belongs to Exponents and logarithms under Number and algebra.
The maximum velocity and acceleration at a direction change are found by differentiating the velocity model; no integration is required.
The binomial distribution is specified and the least n is found from its discrete probabilities; discrete-random-variable work is materially assessed.
The sphere relation is differentiated through the chain rule to obtain dr/dt at the specified volume; this is related-rates/application-of-differentiation work.
The logarithmic curve is inverted and a disk integral in y evaluates the solid of revolution; both integration technique and its application are marked.
Complex modulus/argument is primary, with double-angle identities and the resulting trigonometric equation separately used and marked.
The quotient-rule derivative and local-minimum condition determine the coefficients; graph/transformations are not supported by the mark scheme.
The question explicitly requires derivative and antiderivative calculations; the given formulas do not create separate trig, log or function skills.

Most marks concern discriminants, quadratic conditions and counting coefficient outcomes; the probability model, normal distribution and conditional probability are genuine secondary statistics methods.
The surface/volume optimization is driven by differentiating and interpreting a critical point; algebraic setup is not a separate topic.
The limit, derivative and higher-derivative work directly produces the Maclaurin series; Sequences and series would duplicate the calculus classification.
De Moivre/root calculations and the geometric progression of the complex roots are explicit; trigonometric notation is not a separate assessed identity skill.
Inclusion-exclusion determines the intersection and complements feed the conditional probability; both probability-model and conditional-probability methods are marked.
The triangle side data are used with the cosine rule and a double-angle identity to obtain an exact value; triangle geometry is the adopted primary skill.
The inverse domain requires solving the quadratic inequality and enforcing one-to-one behavior; the inequality is a distinct Number-and-algebra method.
The required range and volume come from a definite integral of secant squared; the geometric setup is an application of integration rather than a separate functions/radian label.
Vector parametrization and scalar products establish the relationships, followed by triangle geometry; no separate trigonometric identity is materially marked.
The proof and solution both use trigonometric identities/equations; induction is not an independently assessed proof topic here.
The endpoint/root/extremum sketch is graph-function work; inverse functions are not required.
The regression fit, extrapolation comment, exponential model interpretation and rate comparison are descriptive modeling/statistics; the exponential form is context.
Vector line equations, minimum distance, plane containment and a line parallel to a plane are all vector/coordinate geometry work; differentiation is unsupported.
Derivative, critical-point and monotonicity work dominate, while asymptotes and sketching graph behavior are independently assessed; the discriminant is intermediate algebra.
Normalization of the pmf and the expectation calculation are discrete-random-variable work; no separate generic probability-model label is needed.
Right-triangle trigonometry and sine/cosine rules determine the requested angles and lengths; coordinate/radian/differentiation labels are unsupported.
The logarithmic domain restriction, discriminant condition and resulting inequality are all explicit marked algebraic methods.
Expectation and the median are obtained by integrating the continuous density; all retained work is owned by continuous random variables.
The marks count arrangements with a restriction and arrangements with a consecutive block; counting and combinatorics is the sole materially assessed method.
